affectedPublicSurfaces: NO seller-facing HTTP surface changes. Nothing under `api/routes/` moves, no `/v1/**` or `/demo/**` response shape changes, no prompt, no playbook, no ToolSpec, no silver/bronze column. This is a CAPTURE slice: its public surface is (a) the contract collection `docs/integrations/tiktok_api/contract-collection.md` and (b) an orders resource reachable on the SANDBOX bundle for the first time. If the executor finds itself editing a route, an ETL transformer or a model, the routing was wrong — stop and report.

The load-bearing code surface is `backend/src/juli_backend/integrations/tiktok/capabilities.py`. VERIFIED against the tree: `SANDBOX_ALLOWED_REQUESTS` contains NO order path of any kind — not `POST /order/\d+/orders/search`, not `GET /order/\d+/orders`. Both calls are therefore refused pre-sign by `SandboxOnlyWriteGuard` today. The diff adds exactly two entries: `("POST", ^/order/\d+/orders/search$)` and `("GET", ^/order/\d+/orders$)`, mirroring the shapes already present on the production-read side (`ORDER_SEARCH_PATH` in `PRODUCTION_READ_POST_PATHS`, `ORDER_DETAIL_PATH` in `PRODUCTION_READ_GET_EXACT`). Nothing else in the tuple moves.

`backend/src/juli_backend/integrations/tiktok/factories.py`: `SandboxWriteResources` is a frozen dataclass holding `inventory`, `products`, `fulfillment`, `promotion` — it has NO `orders` field, which is the second half of why a sandbox order read is unreachable. The diff adds `orders: OrdersResource` to that dataclass and constructs it in `SandboxWriteClientFactory.create_resources`. `OrdersResource` itself (`resources/orders.py`) already exists and is already bound on `ProductionReadResources`; it is REUSED, not forked. Adding a field to a frozen dataclass is a source-compatible widening — every existing construction site is inside this factory.

Contract collection rows added, each carrying request, sanitized response and an environment line naming the shop it came from: an Order List row and an Order Detail row for an AWAITING-SHIPMENT order, plus one PRESENCE TABLE row recording, field by field, whether `rts_sla_time`, `tts_sla_time`, `collection_due_time`, `cancel_order_sla_time`, `fulfillment_type`, `shipping_type`, `delivery_option_id` appeared, and the live `package_status` vocabulary observed. Take the next free A- ids (the collection today runs to A-39 / B-20) and say in the PR which ids were taken. The presence table is committed WHETHER OR NOT the fields are present — an absence recorded is the deliverable.

What the two existing rows actually show, because the issue body overstates it and the executor must not repeat the overstatement: A-4 (`contract-collection.md` ~line 197) and A-5 (~line 220) are both of order `577958834469439754`, status `CANCELLED`. Neither carries `rts_sla_time`, `tts_sla_time`, `collection_due_time`, `cancel_order_sla_time`, `shipping_type` or `delivery_option_id`. But A-4 DOES already carry `fulfillment_type: FULFILLMENT_BY_SELLER`, `delivery_type: HOME_DELIVERY` and a `warehouse_id` — the scope-verification report says so explicitly (`scope-verification/process-order-replenish.md` PO-FR-1: "`fulfillment_type` is in the raw capture (`contract-collection.md:215`)"). A-5 does not carry it. So the new capture must record `fulfillment_type` as CONFIRMED-on-list / TO-BE-CHECKED-on-detail, not as newly discovered.

Environment: the capture is taken on SANDBOX_VN, shop id `7494751643546977923`, authorization id `7658096633384781588`, the Core Function development shop `juliai-test` — recorded on the row. THE FALLBACK IS EXPLICIT AND BOUNDED: this slice is blocked by #1718, the HITL question of whether the sandbox can hold orders at all. If #1718 concludes it cannot, the capture is taken against a PRODUCTION READ of a real awaiting-shipment order through `ProductionReadResources.orders`, the response is redacted of buyer PII before commit, and the row's environment line says PRODUCTION plainly. Sandbox orders are NEVER invented to make the row look cleaner (epic Architect lock).

State written at the vendor: NONE. Both calls are reads (`POST /order/{v}/orders/search` is a search, which is why it already sits in `PRODUCTION_READ_POST_PATHS` beside `products/search`). No order is created, shipped, cancelled or modified anywhere in this journey.
Mixed-version hazard: none. The capture is driven by an operator script against the guarded resource, not by `juli-api` or `juli-celery-worker`, so no process needs restarting for the capture itself.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: the sandbox keeps refusing both order paths pre-sign exactly as today, `SandboxWriteResources` keeps its current four fields, and Process Order stays v2 by S-NFR-10's own rule because its first read is uncaptured on the sandbox. No new exposure, nothing partially applied, no data hazard. Nothing was written at the vendor at any point, so there is nothing to unwind.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the commit. The rollback is a plain code revert: removing the two allowlist entries and the `orders` field from `SandboxWriteResources` returns the guard and the factory to today's exact behaviour, and no caller exists yet to break — the sandbox orders binding has zero call sites in this slice by design. The committed contract rows are ADDITIVE documentation; an observed shape stays true after a code revert, so leaving them in place is correct, and if they are reverted too nothing in the running system notices. Redeploy of the previous release plus a restart of `juli-api` and `juli-celery-worker` is sufficient and NO downgrade is required, because there is no schema change. There is no vendor-side effect a revert fails to undo: every call in this journey was a read.

B-16's example (`contract-collection.md` ~line 1409, 'no live sandbox data available at capture time') is exactly the failure this epic exists to end.

Do NOT invent a sandbox order. If #1718 concludes the sandbox cannot hold orders, the capture is a PRODUCTION READ with the response redacted, and the row's environment line says so — an epic-level Architect lock. Seeding, faking, or hand-authoring a sandbox order to produce a cleaner row is forbidden.

Do NOT commit buyer PII. `recipient_address`, `buyer_email`, buyer phone and any full address are `[REDACTED]` before commit, exactly as A-4 and A-5 already do. This is unconditional and applies whether the capture came from the sandbox or from production.

An ABSENT field becomes a CONFLICT ROW, never an assumption. If `rts_sla_time`, `tts_sla_time`, `collection_due_time`, `cancel_order_sla_time`, `shipping_type` or `delivery_option_id` is missing from the capture, file a documentation-conflict row in PLAN.md §14 with a safe bound and record the absence in the presence table. Do NOT restate the issue body's claim that both existing captures lack `fulfillment_type`. A-4 already carries `fulfillment_type: FULFILLMENT_BY_SELLER` and `delivery_type: HOME_DELIVERY`; `scope-verification/process-order-replenish.md` PO-FR-1 says so.
